title: Variables, Data Types & Agent State Schemas
why: AI agents pass dynamic conversation messages, tool schemas, token counts, and state dictionaries through their workflow graph. Understanding exact data types avoids runtime schema mismatch failures.
objectives: Understand primitive types: int, float, str, bool
Type hints and runtime type checking
concept: An agent state typically consists of strings (system prompts, user inputs), lists (chat history), booleans (should_continue flag), and integers (step count to prevent infinite loops).

code.content:
from typing import TypedDict, List

class AgentState(TypedDict):
    session_id: str
    user_prompt: str
    chat_history: List[dict]
    max_steps: int
    current_step: int
    is_finished: bool

# Initialize state
initial_state: AgentState = {
    'session_id': 'sess_992',
    'user_prompt': 'Analyze today market trends',
    'chat_history': [],
    'max_steps': 5,
    'current_step': 0,
    'is_finished': False
}

print(f'State initialized for step: {initial_state["current_step"]}/{initial_state["max_steps"]}')

practice.description: Define a custom TypedDict for an email-drafting agent with sender, recipient, subject, draft_body, and sent status.
practice.hint: Import TypedDict from typing and define each key with appropriate types.

requirements: Implement a function that updates step count and marks is_finished when current_step >= max_steps

checklist: Mastered Python basic types and typing hints
Understood TypedDict for structured dictionary shapes
Created an immutable state transition check
mistakes: Mutating global state dictionaries directly across multiple concurrent agent tasks
